text:
sanjay: Heads up — after running quantized v1.3 on the convqa suite, pass@5 dropped from 0.62 to 0.48 but BERTScore barely moved. Anyone seen this pattern? Also the CI runner (eval-ci) errored on one of the sampling scripts this morning.

tara: Do you mean our deterministic pass@k estimator or the Monte Carlo sampler? We switched to the fast estimator last week.

sanjay: Fast estimator — yes. I re-ran with exact sampling (100 seeds) and pass@5 goes back to 0.61. So estimator bug? But why is BERTScore stable?

eva: BERTScore is less sensitive to sampling variance for QA since candidate answers often overlap token-wise. pass@k depends on sampling diversity; quantization can change the model's entropy which breaks the fast estimator's assumptions.

sanjay: I dug into the runner logs — bench-bot shows a soft-fail in the sampler: 'RandomState not seeded per-thread'. bench-bot logs show different seeds per process which explains nondeterminism.

bench-bot: automated: found 2 instances of numpy.random.RandomState() without explicit seed in eval_runner/sampling.py: lines ~47 and ~89. Suggest replacing with np.random.default_rng(seed) and passing deterministic seeds from the harness.

tara: Thanks @bench-bot. Also, CI job 'eval-ci' flaps because parallel pytest triggers non-deterministic pass@k. We should pin RNGs and make the fast estimator detect low-entropy cases and fall back to exact sampling.

sanjay: Proposed quick fix: change sampling.py to use default_rng seeded from the test id. Patch snippet: ```python
import hashlib, numpy as np
def seeded_rng(test_id):
    seed = int(hashlib.sha1(test_id.encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % (2**32)
    return np.random.default_rng(seed)
# then use rng.choice(...) for sampling
```

eva: Also update metric impl: pass_at_k currently counts raw exact matches. For QA we want normalized text before exact match: lowercase, strip, collapse whitespace, unicode NFKC. Without that normalization quantization-related tokenization shifts cause false negatives.

tara: Will add normalizer. For BLEU/ROUGE use sacrebleu/rouge-score canonicalization. BERTScore: confirm we use IDF=False and lang='en' — that's currently in metrics/config.json.

sanjay: CI wiring: add a gating job 'eval-metrics-smoke' that runs a small deterministic seed set on PRs for quantization and sampling changes. Example YAML: ```yaml
name: eval-metrics-smoke
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: run smoke script
        run: ./scripts/run_eval_smoke.sh
```

ci-bot: ci-bot: created draft GH workflow branch refs/heads/ci/eval-smoke-171950 and queued run https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/runs/12345 (smoke run queued).

eva: For dashboarding: add 'pass@k_confidence' panel that plots mean and 95% CI across seeds, and a reliability diagram panel for calibration (expected vs observed confidence). Include per-model and per-quantization-version breakdown.

tara: :thumbsup: I'll submit a PR with sampling seed, normalizer, and unit tests that assert deterministic pass@k on a tiny fixture. Sanjay, can you add the dashboard panel config?

sanjay: On it. I'll also add a short note in the eval-harness onboarding: 'When bringing up quantized variants, always run exact-sampling smoke before trusting fast estimators.'

bench-bot: automated: created issue #412 'deterministic-sampling-and-normalizer' and assigned to @tara, @sanjay.

eva: One more ask — update the README to include exact vs approximate pass@k math and link to the paper that justifies our fallback threshold (Wang et al., 2019). Add a short paragraph on calibration: binning strategy and expected sample sizes per bin.

sanjay: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll re-run the convqa quantized job after the PR merges and post results here.
